desc:
Two texts s and t were typed on a keyboard. A lowercase letter types that letter, and the character # is the backspace key, which deletes the character just before the cursor. Pressing backspace when the text is empty does nothing.

Return true if the two final texts are equal, otherwise false. Two empty final texts are equal.

For example, "ab#c" and "ad#c" both end as "ac" (true); "a##c" and "#a#c" both end as "c" (true); "a#c" ends as "c" but "b" ends as "b" (false).

Try to solve it with O(1) extra space.
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase letters and '#'
hints: Building both final texts with a stack and comparing them is easy. How could you compare without building them?
A backspace only affects characters before it, so scanning from the end of each string tells you which characters survive.

Scan both strings from the right with a pointer each. While scanning, keep a counter of pending backspaces: a # increases it, a letter with a pending backspace is skipped and decreases it. Compare the next surviving letters of both strings.
editorial: Processing from the right means every backspace is seen before the characters it deletes. For each string keep a pointer and a count skip of backspaces still to be applied. A helper moves the pointer to the next surviving letter: on # do skip += 1; on a letter with skip > 0 do skip -= 1; otherwise the letter survives.

Advance both pointers to their next surviving letters, then compare. If one string has run out while the other has not, or the letters differ, the answer is false. If both run out together, the answer is true. This takes O(n + m) time and O(1) extra space; the stack version has the same time but O(n + m) space.
